g10-economics-ue4-t1.overview: Perfectly Competitive Markets sits inside Market Structure. Market structures are the focus of Unit 4 of Grade 10 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it examines perfect competition and its many small firms. Then it turns to pure monopoly, a single seller with market power. Next, it covers monopolistic competition, with many firms and differentiated products. Finally, it looks at oligopoly, a market of a few large firms. For each type, it studies the characteristics and the demand and revenue curves. Students will also learn how market structures shape real-life pricing and output.
objectives: Explain the characteristics of the four market structures.
Compare the demand and revenue curves of a firm in each market.
List the sources of monopoly power.
Calculate total, average, and marginal revenue.
Describe how market structures affect price and output.
g10-economics-ue4-t1.simple:
Perfectly Competitive Markets in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the characteristics of perfect competition: many firms, identical products, and free entry.
  • Then the firm as a price taker.
  • Also the demand and revenue curves, where price equals marginal revenue.
g10-economics-ue4-t1.detailed:
Perfectly Competitive Markets — the essentials. First, the characteristics of perfect competition: many firms, identical products, and free entry. Then the firm as a price taker. Also the demand and revenue curves, where price equals marginal revenue.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the characteristics of the four market structures.
  • Compare the demand and revenue curves of a firm in each market.
  • List the sources of monopoly power.
  • Calculate total, average, and marginal revenue.
  • Describe how market structures affect price and output.
